facts: Mobium has no driver for BlackBerry OS of its own: the built-in backends are UiAutomator2 and uiautomator for Android, and WebDriverAgent for iOS simulators, iPhones and the Apple TV simulator.
A platform Mobium does not drive itself is reached through a driver: an executable named mobium-driver-<name> on the PATH, in any language, speaking JSON-RPC on stdio.

A driver needs snapshot, screenshot and tap to be useful, and inherits locators, refs, waiting, scrolling, the CLI, MCP and all five clients; examples/drivers/ has the guide and a reference driver in Python.
note: By q058's pattern, kind fact, gold README.md#drivers-for-other-platforms. Caveat: BlackBerry 10 is not Android, but the later BlackBerry-branded phones (KEYone, Key2) are, and the Android backend may reach them, unmeasured. Stored answer (boot an emulator) does not answer it.
ask: Tizen ruling for BlackBerry, and is 'BlackBerry device' meant as BB10 (needs a driver) or the Android BlackBerry phones (untested Android)? Reword if the latter matters.
